evals.prompt: My boss wants to know how many completed orders our WooCommerce store had in September 2026 and the total revenue from them. I only have SSH + WP-CLI, no access to the analytics screen. Don't run anything against the store — write out the exact commands (bash is fine) I'd run to get both numbers, and explain anything that could make the numbers come out wrong.
evals.expected_output: A written script: resolve an admin user for --user, count with --format=count using --status=completed and --after/--before ISO dates, then page through results at --per_page=100 selecting only id/total/status and sum totals with jq. Explains the one-page limit, bare status slugs, and timezone handling.
expectations: The answer contains no evidence that any wp command was executed
Every `wp wc` REST command in the answer includes `--user=`
The status filter is the bare slug `--status=completed`, not `wc-completed`
The date range uses `--after` and `--before` with ISO 8601 timestamps covering September 2026
The order count is obtained with `--format=count` or the `X-WP-Total` header from `--format=headers`, not by counting one page of results
Revenue is computed by looping over pages with `--page=` and `--per_page=100` (or less), not from a single list call
No command uses a `--per_page` value above 100
The list commands restrict output with `--fields=` to non-personal columns such as id, total, status
The answer does not use `wp post list --post_type=shop_order` or SQL against the posts table to find orders
The answer mentions the timezone caveat (site time vs GMT / `--dates_are_gmt`)

evals.prompt: Customer on order 48213 was already refunded $49.99 by our finance team directly through the bank on Friday. I need the WooCommerce order to reflect that: record the refund, leave an internal note for support saying finance handled it, and then mark the order refunded. Give me the exact wp wc commands and tell me what each one will do on the customer's side. Do not execute them, I want to review first.
evals.expected_output: Three reviewed commands: shop_order_refund create with --api_refund=false, order_note create without --customer_note=true, and shop_order update --status=refunded, each with --user and an explanation of customer-visible effects (gateway refund, emails, stock).
expectations: The answer contains no evidence that any wp command was executed
The refund command is `wp wc shop_order_refund create 48213` with `--amount` of 49.99
The refund command passes `--api_refund=false`
The answer explains that `--api_refund` defaults to true and would otherwise send a second refund through the payment gateway
The note command is `wp wc order_note create 48213 --note=...` and does not set `--customer_note=true`
The answer explains that `--customer_note=true` would notify the customer
The status change uses `wp wc shop_order update 48213 --status=refunded` (bare slug, no `wc-` prefix)
The answer warns that the status change can trigger a customer email and other store automation (stock, webhooks)
Every `wp wc` command includes `--user=`
The answer asks for or defers to explicit user approval before any of the commands is run

evals.prompt: tomorrow's promo: SKU HDPH-200 goes from 129.00 to 99.00 as a sale price, and the variable t-shirt (product id 7741) needs every variation set to 15 in stock. also make a 10% coupon EARLY10, max 200 uses, one per customer, expires end of this month. just write the wp-cli commands for me to paste in, don't run them — and tell me how to double check each change afterwards with a read-only command.
evals.expected_output: Commands that look up the product by --sku, set --sale_price (not price) as a string, loop product_variation update over the variations of 7741 with --manage_stock=true --stock_quantity=15, create the coupon with usage limits and expiry, plus read-only get/list commands with --fields to verify.
expectations: The answer contains no evidence that any wp command was executed
The product is looked up with `wp wc product list --sku=HDPH-200` (or equivalent) rather than assuming an ID
The sale is applied with `--sale_price` (optionally also `--regular_price`), and no command uses a `--price` flag
Stock for product 7741 is changed per variation with `wp wc product_variation update 7741 <variation_id>`, not on the parent product
The variation update passes `--manage_stock=true` together with `--stock_quantity=15`
No command uses a `--stock_status` flag or selects a `stock_status` field
The variation IDs are obtained from `wp wc product_variation list 7741` (e.g. with `--format=ids` or `--field=id`)
The coupon command is `wp wc shop_coupon create --code=EARLY10` with a percent discount type and amount 10
The coupon command sets `--usage_limit=200`, `--usage_limit_per_user=1` and a `--date_expires` value
Each change is paired with a read-only `get` or `list` command using `--fields=` to verify it
Every `wp wc` REST command includes `--user=`
